heroLead: Slippery Rock is best known as a college town, but the farmland ringing the borough in Butler County has real wet-gas Marcellus history, and a lot of the mineral rights here belong to families who farmed this ground long before the university grew into the area's biggest employer.
intro: We hear from Slippery Rock-area families who've held onto mineral rights through a lot of change in this part of Butler County — farms sold for development, the university expanding, new construction on what used to be open fields. Through all of that, the mineral rights underneath often stayed with the original family, separate from whatever happened at the surface.

sections.heading: Farmland Turned Campus Town, Minerals Held Separate
paragraphs: As Slippery Rock grew around the university, a lot of surface transactions left mineral rights reserved to the selling family, which means there may be more mineral-only owners in this area than in a typical rural Butler County township. We check the recorded deed history to confirm whether that's the case for your family's tract.

Butler County has consistent wet-gas Marcellus activity, and land near Slippery Rock has seen its share of leasing over the years, though value still depends on your specific parcel's relationship to active units.

sections.heading: Getting a Clear Number Without the Runaround
paragraphs: We confirm your fractional interest through the Butler County recorder of deeds, check current activity nearby, and give you a straightforward cash offer, handling the closing paperwork ourselves once you're ready to move forward.
